topic: Claude's four ways to remember how you work (custom instructions, projects, connectors, skills), explained like you're five
audience: Professionals who use Claude but repeat themselves in every chat
goal: Put each instruction in the right place, using the free guide on mojeedabisiga.com/learn
notes: From the guide Skill, project, instructions or connector?: custom instructions hold general preferences and apply to every conversation (put: how plain the language, how long answers, words you never want; don't put: steps of one particular job). Example: 'Write in plain English. Keep answers short. Ask me before you assume anything about my work.'

Projects hold background documents and knowledge, and apply only to chats inside that project (files for one client, one course, one big piece of work). Don't put a job you repeat everywhere in a project. Example: 'Using the files here, summarise what changed this month.'

Connectors (MCP) give Claude access to other apps and data such as your drive or calendar, and apply when Claude needs that app. A connector gives access; it doesn't teach Claude how you want a job done.

Skills: a way of doing one particular job, applying only when a request needs it, in any chat. A small folder of instructions (sometimes scripts and templates) with a name and a description; Claude reads the description to decide when to use it. Skills load in layers, so many don't slow Claude down. Rule: once you've explained the same thing three times, make it a skill.

Turn skills on: Settings → Capabilities → 'Create and edit files'. Install: Customize → Skills → + → Create skill → Upload a skill. Name a skill in your request to be sure: 'Use my weekly-report skill on these notes.'
They work together: a connector reaches your project tracker, a skill teaches how your team writes tickets, instructions keep the tone plain, a project holds the background.

The two questions: 1) Is it a way of doing one particular job? No, and it applies everywhere: custom instructions; no, and it's background for one piece of work: a project. 2) Have you explained it three times? Not yet: just ask; yes: make it a skill. Need another app: add a connector.
Mojeed's mission: to make data and AI easy for everyone.
Mojeed's free guides are at https://mojeedabisiga.com/learn (the pages are listed in learn_catalog.json).
